paper_id: DeepWear_ Adaptive Local Offloading for On-Wearable Deep Learning
title: DeepWear: Adaptive Local Offloading for On-Wearable Deep Learning
motivation: Wearables have constrained hardware but need DL; cloud offloading costs privacy and connectivity
problem_framing: Binary offloading decision insufficient; must partition DL model across wearable-handheld
key_insight: Internal layers produce smaller intermediate data, reducing Bluetooth transfer delay
method_signature: Context-aware partial model partition with runtime decision making
evaluation_criteria: End-to-end latency and energy consumption on both wearable and handheld
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Memory usage not considered; only 3 devices and 8 models tested
evidence_for_taste: internal layer inside the model may yield a smaller intermediate output
layers of a given type within the DL model can have significantly different characteristics
DeepX targets at only linear DNN models
offloading decisions are often manually defined at the design time
thinking_moves: 把binary offloading decision扩展为partial offloading问题
通过实验揭示layer-level granularity的性能差异
承认现有function-level offloading方法的根本局限
